definition: The tiny, dense, positively charged centre of an atom, made of protons and neutrons, which holds almost all of the atom's mass.
A particle found in a nucleus: a proton or a neutron.
The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus, symbol $A$, written at the top left of the chemical symbol.
The number of protons in a nucleus, symbol $Z$, written at the bottom left of the chemical symbol; it decides which element the atom is.
Alpha particles fired at thin gold foil mostly passed straight through, but a very few bounced back, showing that an atom is mostly empty space around a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.
